sentences.text:
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioners are before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail in the event of their arrest by the respondent- Police for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC') and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (for short 'DP Act'), on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant-Saima Javd.
2. Heard Sri.Ananda.V., learned counsel for the petitioners and Smt.K.P.Yashodha, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
NC: 2024:KHC:21218 "Whether the petitioners are entitled for grant of bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 4. The petitioners are seeking anticipatory bail on apprehension of being arrested.
It is stated that the wife of petitioner No.1 lodged the complaint, which was later transferred to D.J.Halli Police Station.
But it is stated that till date, no FIR is registered.
Petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are the mother and sister of petitioner No.1.

Since in the first information, which is stated to have been lodged by the wife of petitioner No.1, there are allegations regarding commission of the offences under Section 498A r/w Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of DP Act, the petitioners are apprehending their arrest.
Admittedly, no FIR is registered till date.
Taking into consideration these facts and Syed Zeeshan Ahmed vs The State Of Karnataka on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39962051/

sentences.text: 2 circumstances, I am of the opinion that the apprehension expressed by the petitioners are genuine and they are entitled for grant of pre-arrest protection.
Reasonable conditions may be imposed against the petitioners for their prompt appearance before the Investigating Officer.

NC: 2024:KHC:21218 The Investigating Officer is at liberty to subject the petitioners for custodial interrogation on registration of the FIR, in case of necessity with the permission of the concerned jurisdictional Magistrate.

5. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.
The petitioners are ordered to be enlarged on bail in the event of their arrest by the respondent-Police Station.

The petitioners are directed to appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of this order and on their appearance, the Investigating Officer shall enlarge them on bail subject to the following conditions:-
a.

The petitioners shall furnish the bond in a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs only) each with two sureties each for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer;
b.

The petitioners shall not commit similar offences;
NC: 2024:KHC:21218 c. The petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer or the court as and when required; and d.
The petitioners shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses.

e. If in case, the Investigating Officer deems it necessary to subject the petitioners for custodial interrogation, he is at liberty to do so on registration of the FIR, with prior permission of the jurisdictional Magistrate.
On furnishing the sureties by the petitioners, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to verify the correctness of the address and authenticity of the documents furnished by them.
On satisfaction of the said documents, he may proceed to accept the sureties within a reasonable time.

Sd/-
